pageCache.pageTitle: Kidbrooke Park Primary School - Aims, Values & Ethos
pageCache.text:
Aims, Values & Ethos
Kidbrooke Park is a values-based learning community dedicated to the whole child. Our aim is to provide an exceptional educational journey that equips your child with the skills needed for lifelong success and learning.
Our Kidbrooke Park Values are:
These values are reinforced through everything we do, including rights-respecting assemblies, the PSHE curriculum, and daily classroom interactions, where they are visibly displayed and actively referred to as an integral part of our learning environment.
We believe these values not only support academic success but also prepare our children for all aspects of life.
In addition to our values, we focus on developing key learning dispositions or 'habits of mind' - behaviour essential for successful learners. This year, we emphasise fostering independent, aspirational and adventurous learners. These dispositions are modelled by our staff and reinforced through carefully planned opportunities each day.
At Kidbrooke Park, our ethos is rooted in creating a nurturing, inclusive environment where every child is valued and supported in their personal and academic growth. We are committed to developing confident, resilient, and compassionate learners who are equipped with the skills, values and mindset needed to succeed in an ever-changing world. Our ethos emphasises a strong sense of community, collaboration, and respect, ensuring every child feels empowered to reach their full potential.

pageCache.pageTitle: Kidbrooke Park Primary School - Welcome From our Head of school
pageCache.text:
Welcome From our Head of school
Welcome to Kidbrooke Park Primary School. It is a real privilege to be the Head of School and to lead such a caring, inclusive and aspirational community in the Royal Borough of Greenwich.
At Kidbrooke Park, children are at the heart of everything we do. I believe deeply that every child deserves to feel safe, valued, inspired to learn and that strong relationships are the foundation of success. Our school values shape daily life here — guiding how we learn, how we treat one another and how we develop as confident, respectful and responsible individuals.
We are proud of our broad, balanced and well-sequenced curriculum, which is carefully designed to meet the needs of all learners and help children build knowledge and skills over time. High-quality texts, purposeful learning experiences and opportunities beyond the classroom bring learning to life and support children to achieve well. We make the most of our local area and school environment, and our children take great pride in their learning spaces and the work they produce.
Our dedicated and skilled staff team share high expectations for every child and a strong commitment to inclusion and excellence. Working in close partnership with families and as part of our wider trust, we value collaboration, reflection and continuous improvement. This ensures that our practice is strong, our provision is responsive and our children are well prepared for the next stage of their education.
Thank you for taking the time to visit our website. We are proud of our school and would warmly welcome you to come and see Kidbrooke Park Primary School in action.
Head of School Muneera Najak

pageCache.text:
Kidbrooke Park Learning Centre
Welcome to the Kidbrooke Park Learning Centre (KPLC) – we hope this website helps you find the information you need and that it gives you a taste of life at our centre.
Many of our pupils have previously found school a challenge. Our mission is to help every child become an independent, lifelong learner who can regulate and manage their own feelings and behaviour.
At KPLC, the experiences and individual needs of our children are at the heart of everything we do. We are passionate about ensuring that each child is understood, valued and supported to thrive.
Our dedicated staff are committed to supporting the wellbeing and progress of every child, creating a safe, caring and inclusive environment where each pupil can reach their full potential. In return, our pupils show mutual respect, build positive relationships and demonstrate perseverance and resilience every day.
Our centre has been recognised for its commitment to inclusive and supportive practice. KPLC has been awarded the prestigious ADHD Friendly School Award and has achieved the standards set by the Autism Education Trust. We also embed Trauma Informed Practices across our provision and have a dedicated on-site Trauma and Mental Health Schools Practitioner. In addition, we are proud to have received a commendation in the ARC Alex Thimpson Award by the Attachment Research Community, highlighting our strong commitment to relational practice and inclusion.
We believe children achieve their best when home and school work in partnership, building strong relationships with families based on trust, respect and open communication.
By working together, we aim to give our pupils the opportunity to grow in confidence and develop tolerance, understanding, independence, positive relationships and, above all, a lifelong positive attitude towards learning.
Thank you for visiting our website. If you would like any further information, please do not hesitate to get in touch using our contact details.
Alexandra Connolly – Head of KPLC

Clubs
Here at Kidbrooke Park we offer a breakfast club provision for all children to promote good punctuality and to offer extended care from 7:50am to 9am. Please speak to the school office for more information.
Places are on a first come, first served basis. Therefore, if your child does not wish to attend a club for any reason, please let the school office know so that the place can be opened up to another child who is on the waiting list.
We are delighted to work in partnership with MSE play who now provide our extended day service from 3.30pm until 6.30pm. For more information, please visit their website.
In order to reinforce the positive view of school our children already have, and to develop social skills and to teach specific skills, we run a number of after-school clubs for children at Kidbrooke Park Primary School.
The clubs last from 3.30pm to 4.30pm and are run by our staff or coaches well known to us. The range of clubs changes each term so that children can experience different activities and to reflect current interests. Our clubs might be sporting, creative, or based on games or hobbies. Some clubs may result in performances or competitive matches.
Autumn Term After School Clubs 2026
To sign your child up to any of our clubs, please head to the 'after-school club' tab on your My Child At School App.
Wave Coaching is an after school football club that takes place every Wednesday from 3.30pm to 4.30pm for children in Years 1 - 6, for more information and to book a place for your child, please use the link below.

Curriculum
The Compass Curriculum is inclusive of, and builds upon, the EYFS curriculum (please find more information about our EYFS curriculum under the EYFS tab in this section) and the National Curriculum, and maximises cross-curricular opportunities and the fluent use of English and Maths to enhance progress for everyone. Our curriculum complies with our duties in the Equality Act 2010 and the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014 to ensure our curriculum is accessible for those with disabilities or special educational needs. For further information, please see the SEND page on this website.
Our curriculum is designed by our Subject Leaders who map progression in both substantive and disciplinary knowledge for Reading, Writing, Maths, Science, Computing and Foundation Subjects across Key Stage One and Key Stage Two. Knowledge is purposefully planned across our Frameworks providing opportunities for knowledge to build on prior learning and to be revisited in subsequent years and in different subjects so that knowledge is deepened and mastered over time.
Our Curriculum is designed to narrow the gap for children who are disadvantaged and sets out purposefully sequenced knowledge, vocabulary and skills for each subject and each year group so that children know more and remember more overtime. Key foundational knowledge such as phonics, handwriting and number sense are taught systematically in the Early Years and throughout Year 1. We teach to support children to keep up from the start and close any learning gaps quickly, using targeted keeping up sessions to ensure that all children especially those disadvantaged have the key knowledge that they need to access the wider curriculum. At Compass, this is an issue of equity and social justice and is key in our drive to narrow the disadvantaged gap and ensure all children thrive.
Knowing More and Remembering More
Our curriculum is ambitious for our children. Each year, deep knowledge and memory of key concepts is supported through making meaningful connections both between and across subject domains. Through making connections and applying learnt knowledge to solve problems and answer big questions, children learn to respond to increasingly challenging problems and questions confidently as well as knowing more and remember more overtime.
Our Curriculum aims to support children to be confident, independent, and inquisitive learners, who develop an understanding of the world – past, present, and future. The curriculum is designed to support children in the acquisition of desirable learning dispositions through providing contextualised learning experiences and teaching that enable them to understand fully what they need to know and how they need to be successful learners.
The foreign language taught in KS2 is French.
Whole School Projects provide a further inspirational context for learning and provide opportunities to show progression in learning across the school. These are planned yearly and include projects based on paintings by artists across the world, places of interest, current day events from around the world and high-quality texts and picture books. Each year group will develop a scheme of work to develop the learning for each project in the way most relevant and stimulating for their children.

Parents can request for their child to be removed from all or some RE sessions, although we would appreciate a conversation with parents who may be considering this. Learning about each other's differences is crucial in today's world.

SEND Local Offer
At Compass, we are proud to be inclusive schools that are committed to learning for all. The principles of inclusion and diversity underpin all that we do. We respect and value difference, and we are committed to ensuring that every member of our school community feels a sense of belonging within the school and wider community and to know that they are respected and able to participate fully in school life. Through inclusion, all adults ensure appropriate learning and positive experiences for all our pupils. All children share a common entitlement to a broad and balanced curriculum which meets their social and learning needs.
At Kidbrooke Park Primary School, the Inclusion team is led by Emma Dale-Emberton. You can contact them by calling 020 8856 8315. Our SEND information report provides further details about how we meet the needs of children with a special education need in our schools.
Information about the wider support available in the Royal Borough of Greenwich can be found on the Local Offer website.

pageCache.pageTitle: Kidbrooke Park Primary School - Pupil & Sports Premium
pageCache.text:
Pupil & Sports Premium
WHAT IS THE PUPIL PREMIUM?
The Pupil Premium provides additional funding on top of the main funding a school receives. It is targeted at students from disadvantaged backgrounds to ensure they benefit from the same opportunities as pupils from less deprived families. The premium goes to students who are currently on Free School Meals (FSM) or have been registered for (FSM) in the past six years. Pupils in care and pupils who have been looked after by local authorities for more than six months also continue to qualify for the Pupil Premium.
WHY IS THERE A PUPIL PREMIUM?
Pupils who have been eligible for Free School Meals at any point in their school career have consistently lower educational attainment than those who have never been eligible. In 2009-10 GCSE statistics showed that around a third of students who have been on Free School Meals in the previous six years achieved five or more A*- C grades, compared to more than two thirds of their fellow students.
HOW WILL THE IMPACT OF THE SPENDING OF THE PUPIL PREMIUM BE MEASURED?
At Kidbrooke Park Primary School, the usual cycle of data collection and the monitoring and tracking of attainment will be used to inform progress and enable the early identification of need, support and appropriate intervention.
Schools receive designated pupil premium funding to support vulnerable children within the school. Schools are free to decide how to allocate this funding to best support and raise the attainment for the most vulnerable pupils.
Sports Premium
The government provides additional funding to improve provision of physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools. This funding - provided jointly by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport – is allocated to primary school Head Teachers. The money must be used to improve the provision of P.E. and school sport.
Please click here to access the government website: www.gov.uk/government/school-pe-and-sport-funding

They are the voice of all pupils at Kidbrooke Park Primary and take their role extremely seriously. We elect new members via a secret ballot during the Autumn Term.
Our Year 6 representatives are also part of our Compass Council who meet throughout the year in various locations.
We are proud to have achieved the Travel for Life Gold Award from TFL!
In October 2025, Kidbrooke Park received the Travel for Life Gold accreditation, recognising our outstanding commitment to promoting active, responsible and sustainable travel among pupils, staff and families.
